bounded_question: What does node #94 function 0x514f270 do with its outer object and flag byte: under which two mutexes, with which thresholds, when does it rebuild the snapshot at inner+0x188 via 0x514ed50 versus only incrementing its +0x124 field, how are its clock (+0x98) and consumer (+0xb8) dispatch chains walked, and what does it publish under the second lock?

counter_inc.scope_note: cited as a callee only; the accessor trio 0x514df30/0x514df40/0x514df50 is not otherwise modelled here

ctor.scope_note: cited as a callee only; the two code addresses it stores are recorded verbatim, not interpreted

entries.a_unlock_entry_action: unlocks mutex A (r13) via pthread_mutex_unlock, checks the canary, then _Unwind_Resume with the exception object in rbx
entries.both_unlock_entry_action: unlocks mutex B (rbx, the inner object) via pthread_mutex_unlock, restores the exception object from rbp into rbx, then falls into the A-unlock entry

cleanup_routine.scope_note: the FDE immediately preceding the window (0x514f224..0x514f26d); it is the window's exception consumer, not claimed as a standalone function window

clock_chain.links: +0x20 from each wrapper to the next wrapper
clock_chain.rule: the head wrapper's inner +0x98 slot is compared against cell 0x5777bc8; while it equals the cell the walk advances via +0x20, comparing each further slot against the first slot value (which provably equals the cell on skipped paths); at most three comparisons, and the fourth node is called unconditionally; the result is the clock value

composed_rule: the window takes (outer rdi, flag byte sil); inner = [outer+0x128]; a null inner returns immediately with no lock taken

mutex A is inner+0x160 (locked first, unlocked last via a tail jump) and mutex B is the inner object itself (locked after the snapshot/skip decision, unlocked before A); a nonzero lock result throws a system error via _ZSt20__throw_system_errori@plt after the canary check

thresholds depend on the flag byte: flag 0 gives count limit 500 and time limit 180000000; any nonzero flag gives count limit 10 and time limit 10000000; the limits are built with the sbb/and/add sequence (count mask 0x1ea + 10, time mask 0xa21fe80 + 0x989680)

stale adjustment, before the clock dispatch: when inner+0x2c0 < inner+0x2c8, the time limit becomes max(time limit, (inner+0x2c8 - inner+0x2c0) * count limit), then control re-enters the dispatch check

clock dispatch: the +0x98 chain (head [inner+0x2d8], sentinel cell 0x5777bc8, +0x20 links, at most 4 nodes, fourth unconditional) yields the clock value; elapsed = clock value - inner+0x2c8 (unsigned wrap as written)
decision: the snapshot is rebuilt exactly when elapsed > time limit; otherwise the skip path runs

snapshot path: inner+0x2c0 is set to the clock value, then 0x514ed50 builds the snapshot at inner+0x188 from source wrapper [inner+0x2d0] and the elapsed value; the consumer struct is then built at rsp+0x10 by 0x514def0 (snapshot pointer, 0, 0x514b120, 0x514ac60) with a qword 0x100 at rsp+0x08

consumer dispatch: the +0xb8 chain (head inner [[inner+0x2d0]], sentinel cell 0x5777a50, +0x38 links, at most 11 nodes, eleventh unconditional) is called with (wrapper, struct rsp+0x10, pointer rsp+0x08); after the call, if the struct's +0x10 field ([rsp+0x20]) is nonzero it is called with (struct, struct, 3)
commit path (snapshot path only): the clock head's +0x98 slot is called directly with no chain walk; the fresh value is stored to inner+0x2c8 and, via 0x514df30, to snapshot+0x130
skip path: 0x514df40 adds 1 (32-bit) to snapshot+0x124, then control jumps straight to the publish section, skipping the fresh clock call and the snapshot+0x130 store

publish (under mutex B): the 0x138 bytes at inner+0x188 are copied to inner+0x28, except the string slot at snapshot+0x20 which is copied by _M_assign into inner+0x48 instead of a raw copy; the copy therefore covers snapshot+0x00..+0x138 including the +0x120 counter, the +0x124 field, the +0x128 elapsed value and, on the snapshot path, the +0x130 commit-time value
unlock order: mutex B is unlocked, the canary is checked, then mutex A is unlocked via a tail jump to pthread_mutex_unlock

the function is stack-canary protected (canary slot rsp+0x38, __stack_chk_fail on mismatch) and its exception entries are the three landing stubs at the tail of its own range, jumping into the shared cleanup routine at 0x514f224

consumer_chain.links: +0x38 from each wrapper to the next wrapper
consumer_chain.rule: the head inner's +0xb8 slot is compared against cell 0x5777a50; while it equals the cell the walk advances via +0x38, comparing each further slot against the first slot value (which provably equals the cell on skipped paths); at most ten comparisons, and the eleventh node is called unconditionally; every call passes (wrapper, struct rsp+0x10, pointer rsp+0x08)

landing_stubs.note: each stub is endbr64, then moves the exception object rax to rbx (0x514f6f5, 0x514f701) or to rbp (0x514f70d), then a direct jump into the cleanup routine; the packet does not claim which call site each stub serves, since that mapping lives in the LSDA, not in the window bytes

post_call_callback.condition: [rsp+0x20] (the consumer struct's +0x10 field) nonzero after the consumer dispatch returns
post_call_callback.note: the same call appears in the cleanup routine's full entry, so it runs on the exception path too when the field is nonzero

publish.string_slot: snapshot+0x20 copied by _M_assign@plt (0x56605c0, GOT 0x5779008) from inner+0x1a8 into inner+0x48; all other 16-byte chunks are raw vector copies

thresholds.stale_rule: when inner+0x2c0 < inner+0x2c8, time limit becomes max(time limit, (inner+0x2c8 - inner+0x2c0) * count limit) before the clock dispatch

unknowns: the identity and contents of the outer object, the inner object, the wrappers, the clock object and the consumer chain, and what the published snapshot means to its readers (all values are stored verbatim)
why the flag byte selects (500, 180000000) versus (10, 10000000), and what the flag byte means to the three direct callers (one passes 0, two pass a caller flag byte)
why the stale path inflates the time limit by the timestamp gap times the count limit, and what inner+0x2c0 / inner+0x2c8 measure beyond the observed clock-value arithmetic
what the consumer struct's +0x10 field means when the consumer dispatch leaves it nonzero, and what the (struct, struct, 3) callback does
what the qword 0x100 at rsp+0x08 means to the consumer dispatch
why the commit clock call uses the head's +0x98 slot directly with no chain walk, unlike the decision clock dispatch
which call site each landing stub serves (LSDA mapping, not pinned from the window bytes)
the reaching path beyond the three direct callers: no tail jump or absolute pointer to 0x514f270 exists, so indirect reaching paths are left unclaimed
